issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method has inconsistent parameter lists across artifacts. The problem statement UML and textual instructions (messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]") and the template Main.java call use a no-argument method messageOnRide(). In the solution, Rideable.messageOnRide is declared as messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementations (Pig, Seal) require an int parameter and include speed in the returned string. This mismatch will prevent the template Main code from compiling against the solution API and confuses students about the intended signature/behaviour.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to use a no-argument method: messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (remove the speed parameter and adjust implementations in Pig and Seal), or (B) update the problem statement and template Main.java to require an int speed parameter (document expected behaviour including speed, and call messageOnRide(speed) in Main). Option A is recommended to match the current specification and template usage.
